threads.subject: Guided Reviews in VS Code: spec and prototype
threads.slice: This thread has 140 messages over two days. The tour shows a few of them.
threads.real_answer: A · Our guide reader in one tab

messages.body: Honestly I’m just struggling with this UX. I think using the native VS Code interfaces instead of building what we had designed as our own guide interface was a mistake. Launch an Opus agent to evaluate it and mock up alternatives.

Understood. An Opus agent can evaluate it now: your Plannotator guide reader against the VS Code split, using the real screenshots, with 3 to 4 mocked alternatives and a short honest note on each.

:::question
Start the evaluation with 3 to 4 mockups?
- [ ] Yes, start it
- [ ] Evaluate only, no mockups yet
Recommended: Yes, start it
:::

The evaluation is done. You were right: the native VS Code split is the problem. One guide is spread over six surfaces: three tabs, the sidebar tree, the chapter panel and the Comments panel. The chapter’s “why” sits in a 340 px side panel, away from the code it explains.

**Recommended: A, our own guide reader in one VS Code tab.** Chapters with their prose beside the diffs, the whole chapter in one scroll, and hover and go to definition from VS Code’s real language server. Cost: medium, after a 2-day check that hover feels instant.

:::question
Which direction for the VS Code guide interface?
- [ ] A · Our guide reader in one tab — ![Direction A, mocked in VS Code: our guide reader in one tab](vs-a-thumb.webp) after a 2-day hover-speed check
- [ ] B · Our reader beside a live native diff — ![Direction B, mocked in VS Code: our reader beside a live native diff](vs-b-thumb.webp) two half-width panes, one file at a time
- [ ] C · VS Code’s multi-file diff per chapter — ![Direction C, mocked in VS Code: the multi-file diff per chapter](vs-c-thumb.webp) chapter prose only in a comment box
- [ ] Ship 0.17.0 as is now — and do A as the next version
Recommended: A · Our guide reader in one tab
:::

suggest.phrase: It is also the cheapest direction, because the reader and its hooks already exist.
suggest.comment: Nice, reusing the reader’s hooks keeps this small.

suggest.phrase: a 2-day check that hover feels instant
suggest.comment: Good. If hover isn’t instant, tell me before you build B.

messages.body:
A it is, and it’s recorded as approved. An Opus builder has started.

- **The speed check, first:** our reader in a VS Code tab, measuring hover from VS Code’s real language server. The target is under ~150 ms once warm.
- **Then the build, matching mockups a1–a4:** chapters with their prose beside the diffs in one scroll; hover, go to definition and ⌘-click from VS Code.

You get the speed numbers first, then screenshots, then a review before anything merges.

Direction A is built as PR #2134, and a VS Code test window is opening on this repo with it running.

- **The speed check passed easily:** hover in 7 ms typical, 9 ms at worst, against a 150 ms target.
- **The guide tab:** one tab with our guide reader, each chapter’s text beside its files’ diffs, all in one scroll.
- **Ask:** select lines in a diff and ask; the answer opens beside.

![The guide tab, built](built-a1.webp)
![A chapter, built](built-a2.webp)
